answer.rationale: The p99 write latency spike began 30 minutes after the recent release deployment, indicating a strong causal relationship. Memory_b3 confirms that provisioning headroom normally absorbs peak traffic surges without latency degradation, suggesting the release—not load—is the root cause. Memory_b1 demonstrates that rolling back a problematic release can clear performance issues without customer impact. Given the settlement traffic peak and single-intervention constraint, a full rollback (broad_rollout) is the most reliable path to restore write latency while preserving the ability to roll forward if the diagnosis is incorrect.
